title: Methods for the metrological characterization of wearable devices for the measurement of physiological signals: state of the art and future challenges
author: Cosoli, Antognoli, et al.
materials: correlation between test and reference signals.

steps.title: Prepare Test Population and Ethics
steps.instruction: Recruit a test population and ensure all ethical and legal requirements are met.

substeps.instruction: Define population characteristics including gender, age, weight, height (or BMI), and skin tone.
Obtain signed informed consent from all participants after explaining study aims and modalities.
Ensure compliance with the WMA Declaration of Helsinki and obtain Ethical Committee approval if necessary.

steps.title: Select Reference and Test Devices
steps.instruction: Identify the wearable device under test and a suitable gold standard reference device.

substeps.instruction: Select a reference device with known accuracy (e.g., BioHarness 3.0 with ± 1 bpm accuracy for HR in 0–140 bpm range and 250 Hz sampling frequency).
Ensure the test device is appropriate for the target application (e.g., Samsung Galaxy Watch3 for ECG monitoring).

steps.title: Execute Data Acquisition Protocol
steps.instruction: Perform simultaneous recordings using both the test and reference devices under controlled conditions.

substeps.instruction: Equip the subject with both devices simultaneously.
Perform recordings after physical exertion (e.g., 2-min treadmill at 3, 8, and 10 km/h with 0-slope; 3 recordings).
Ensure all acquisitions are made in static conditions with the subject remaining as still as possible to minimize movement artefacts.

steps.title: Process Physiological Signals
steps.instruction: Apply signal processing algorithms to extract relevant physiological parameters from the raw data.

substeps.instruction: Use the Pan-Tompkins algorithm for R peaks detection in ECG signals.
Derive the tachogram from both the test and reference signals.

steps.title: Perform Metrological Analysis
steps.instruction: Analyze the measurement deviations between the test device and the reference gold standard using statistical methods.

substeps.instruction: Compute measurement deviations (differences between HR measured by test and reference devices).
Analyze the distribution of deviations by calculating the mean (µ) and standard deviation (σ).
Perform an agreement analysis using Bland-Altman plots.
Calculate the Pearson's correlation coefficient to determine the linear correlation between signals.
Determine statistical confidence by calculating the confidence interval (e.g., CI95% using a coverage factor k = 2).
